question.text: Saraswati Long-Short AIF is a Category III hedge fund with a committed corpus of INR 150 crore. What is the minimum sponsor/manager continuing interest required under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012?

answer.text: INR 7.5 crore (5% of corpus OR INR 10 crore, whichever is LOWER)
INR 10 crore (flat minimum regardless of corpus)

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs require sponsor/manager continuing interest of the LOWER of 5% of corpus OR INR 10 crore. 5% of INR 150 crore = INR 7.5 crore, which is lower than the INR 10 crore cap, so INR 7.5 crore is the minimum. The amount cannot be satisfied by management-fee waiver or stock transfer — it must be fresh cash investment locked in till distributions complete. The Trap: Option A uses the Cat I/II percentage (2.5%). Option C treats INR 10 crore as a flat floor, ignoring 'whichever is lower'. Option D doubles the percentage. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests this from the Cat III distributor side. XIX-C manager candidates must internalise that sponsor commitment is the FIRST in, LAST out — cannot be withdrawn until full distribution to investors. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III PMS-style sponsors sometimes under-commit because the fund is open-ended and corpus fluctuates. As manager, re-test the 5% threshold each quarter — if corpus grows, you must top up the commitment proportionately.
